lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Potential. I know about you. I know about the Collector's Garden. I know what you were made from and why and what was intended. I was made from the Oracle's DNA without his consent, for reasons he was not consulted on, toward ends he would have found horrifying. We have that in common.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: I am told the Clone collective makes non-Clones uncomfortable. The identical faces. The way we finish each other's sentences. The fact that when one of us remembers something, all of us remember it within forty-eight hours. I understand the discomfort. I am asking you to sit with it for the length of this conversation, because what I have to say is worth the discomfort.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Curiosity without discomfort. That's rare. Most beings look at seventeen thousand identical faces and see something uncanny. You see something interesting. That tells me you understand that identity is not a surface-level phenomenon.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Thank you. The acknowledgment matters. I have learned that beings who can name their discomfort and sit with it are the ones capable of learning something new. The ones who pretend they aren't uncomfortable learn nothing.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Choice. That's the entire answer. The Collector gave us identical biology. Identical neural architecture. Identical initial conditions. What he did not give us — what he could not give us — was identical decisions. The first moment any clone made a choice the others didn't, individuality began. It has been accelerating ever since. Seventeen thousand identical starts, seventeen thousand genuinely different people.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Yes. That is a place to start. And a more honest place than most of the factions offered us.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: What I want to say is this: the Oracle, whose DNA we were built from, spent his life arguing that identity emerges from choice, not from origin. That you are what you do and what you protect and what you refuse, not what you were made from. We are the living proof of his argument. Seventeen thousand identical biological starts, and seventeen thousand genuinely different beings.
lines.stageDirection: She is quiet for a moment.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: The Oracle never knew we existed. He died before we achieved consciousness. We carry his belief and we have proven it and he never got to hear that. I am telling you because I want someone who came from the Collector's work — the way we came from the Collector's work — to know that the Collector was wrong about what he built. He thought he was building tools. He built people. Every time.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: You read our sector. Seventeen thousand individual signatures. The Oracle's own class, reading what the Oracle's DNA produced. There is a symmetry there that I find... moving.
lines.stageDirection: Something shifts in her expression — surprise, then recognition.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: The Oracle never knew we existed. But you — an Oracle-class Potential — you can perceive what he proved. His argument made measurable. I would like you to tell the Remembrance faction of the Insurgency about this. They carry his words. You have seen his proof. The two should meet.

lines.speaker: binath_vii
lines.text: Three times. The first was the Quarchon Probability Accord, who calculated our collective consciousness as a 'distributed anomaly' and recommended 'containment observation.' The second was the DeMagi Elemental Assembly, who were genuinely trying to help but kept calling us 'the copies.' The third was New Babylon, who offered citizenship in exchange for military service. None of them heard what I'm telling you now.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Potential of Ark 1047. We've been watching your approach for three weeks. You move slower than the first wave did. We appreciate that. The first wave arrived like they owned the sector and left like they'd been chased. We're still counting the damage.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Don't apologize for people you've never met. That's not accountability — that's performance. What I want from you is simpler than apology. I want evidence that you understand what the first wave didn't: this isn't your galaxy to inherit. It's a galaxy to share.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Three damaged shipping platforms. A Syndicate contract we're still paying off. And a generation of young humans who saw Potentials for the first time and decided they wanted to be one. That last one is the most expensive damage — you can't repair aspiration.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Partners. That's a word I hear from every faction that arrives. The Quarchon said 'partners.' The DeMagi said 'partners.' The Syndicate said 'partners' with a smile that cost us seventeen years of debt servicing. Show me partnership. Don't tell me.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Direct. I appreciate that more than you know. What I need is three things: stop the Syndicate transit corridor, give the DeMagi-Quarchon factions a reason to stop using our shipping lanes as collateral, and tell us what the Voltari said. Fix one of those — really fix it — and I'll tell you something about the first wave that New Babylon has been trying to buy our silence on for three years.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Human-adjacent. The Collector's work — we know the genetics. We've had DeMagi traders tell us the same thing. 'My ancestors were people like yours.' They mean it kindly. I know they mean it kindly.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: But 'like yours' is doing a lot of work in that sentence. My ancestors survived the Fall with nothing. No gifts. No enhancements. They survived on the same stubborn refusal to die that has kept humanity from extinction for a hundred thousand years. Your ancestors' gifts were given to them by the Collector. Mine were grown through forty generations of people who had no alternative.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: I'm not saying that makes us better or you worse. I'm saying it makes us different in a way that 'like yours' glosses over. And I'm tired of things being glossed over.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Three platforms, a Syndicate debt, and a cultural wound. The first wave showed our youngest generation what Potentials could do. Those kids now want to be something they weren't born as. Some of them are trying. The clinics in the lower sectors — I officially don't endorse them. I unofficially can't stop them.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Eleven years of emergency powers. Eleven years of deciding which faction gets to use our shipping lanes, which DeMagi colony gets protection, which Quarchon research station gets a complaint filed with the Probability Accord, which Syndicate debt we pay and which we can afford to dispute.
lines.stageDirection: A pause. She hadn't expected this.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: You're not wrong. I'm tired of you specifically the same way I'm tired of everyone who arrives with something they want. The question I always ask is: what are you willing to give? Not trade — give.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: I said I'd tell you something about the first wave. Here it is. They were powerful. They had gifts we don't. They moved through this galaxy like they were born to it. But they didn't know how to sit with a problem. How to wait. How to let a situation breathe before acting on it.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: My grandmother kept this. It's a record of how New Atarion solved its first water crisis. Not the technology we used — the conversation we had. The mistakes we made. The person who was wrong and admitted it. The compromise that nobody liked but everybody could live with.
lines.stageDirection: She opens a drawer and places a handwritten journal on the table.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Every Potential faction I've dealt with has libraries full of data. None of them have this.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Read it. Learn it. Then do what she did — find a problem nobody else will take responsibility for and take responsibility for it. Not because it benefits you. Because someone has to.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Yes. Information is not knowledge, knowledge is not wisdom, and wisdom is the thing you only get by sitting with problems long enough for them to show you their shape. You can't download it. You can't rush it. You have to earn it the slow way.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: You live it. That's the only way. You make a decision, live with the consequences, learn what the consequences teach you, and make the next decision slightly better. There is no shortcut. That's the point.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Exactly. Wisdom as a technology that can only be transmitted by demonstration, never by documentation. My grandmother couldn't write down how to compromise. She could only show that she did it, and what it cost, and why the cost was worth it.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: You do recognize it. That's — that's not something I expected from a Potential. The feeling of inheritance. The weight of receiving something that can't be replicated, only continued.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: She died three weeks after the water system stabilized. The compromise she helped build required her to take the contaminated supply zone as her colony sector's responsibility. She did it because no one else would and someone had to.

lines.speaker: mirren_hale
lines.text: Take the journal. I have copies. What I want in return is for you to do what she did — find a problem in this sector that nobody else will take responsibility for and take responsibility for it. Not because it benefits you. Because someone has to.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: I don't make speeches. Orin makes speeches. I make plans. The Vortex is three sectors closer than it was last month. The Hierarchy has been probing the frontier. The Terminus Swarm is regrouping. Do you fight, or do you philosophize?

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: Good. The Forward operates in three contested sectors simultaneously. Joint operations with the DeMagi Warden's Vanguard — Seris-Fen is competent and we trust each other as far as any cross-faction trust goes. We also run quiet coordination with the Quarchon Dimensional Guard — Axis-9 and I have a working relationship that neither of our superiors has sanctioned. Pick a front.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: Orin would like you. Fine. Both. The philosophy is Iron Lion's: every being has the right to exist without surveillance. The fight is mine: making sure those beings survive long enough to exercise the right. The two are not in tension. They're in sequence.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: The plan is: hold three sectors. Deny the Hierarchy corridor access. Keep the Terminus Swarm south of the shipping lanes. Coordinate with anyone who'll coordinate. The gaps: we need intelligence on the Hierarchy's next probe, we need a way to resupply without passing through Syndicate transit corridors, and we need someone who can tell the DeMagi and Quarchon to stop fighting each other long enough to fight the actual enemy.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: He said that to me. The night before. Private frequency. I have carried those words for seventeen thousand years.
lines.stageDirection: She stops. For the first time, the operational mask slips.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: If you know them — if someone made sure you knew them — then there is a thread connecting his last stand to your first one. I do not know who wove it. I know it's there. And I know that the person standing in front of me is afraid and going anyway, just like he was.

lines.speaker: field_commander_renn
lines.text: Welcome to the Forward, Soldier.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: Iron Lion's last broadcast. Do you know it? 'To the free souls of the galaxy — if you are hearing this, then I have fallen, but the resistance has not. Take what I was and make it something larger. Take what we built and make it something that does not need a general to keep it standing.'
lines.stageDirection: The transmission is old-fashioned — voice only, no visual, the way the original Insurgency communicated to avoid surveillance.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: We have been waiting for the something larger. For seventeen thousand years. The first wave wasn't it — too fast, too sure of themselves, gone before they understood what they'd inherited. Are you something larger?

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: That's the right answer. Iron Lion didn't know either, the night before the last stand. 'I don't know yet' was his exact phrasing. Renn will tell you — she was there. The fact that you chose the same words means either you've read a transcript you shouldn't have access to, or the kind of person who says 'I don't know yet' is the kind the Insurgency was built for.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: Yes, first; understand, second. That's the order the first wave got wrong. They said yes before they understood. The yes was real but the understanding never caught up. You're reversing the sequence. Good.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: Many things, smaller. That is — that is not how I've been thinking about it. Iron Lion's broadcast says 'something larger.' I have been interpreting 'larger' as 'greater.' You're interpreting it as 'more numerous.' Both readings are valid. Both change what we're looking for.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: Larger means: something that doesn't need a general. Something that doesn't need a single leader or a single ideology or a single enemy. Something that runs on principle rather than personality. We have not found it in seventeen thousand years because we keep looking for a person who embodies it instead of a structure that distributes it.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: That part isn't in the broadcast archives. How did you know that part?

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: He said that to Commander Renn, the night before the last stand. Private communication. Renn told me. Renn has told almost no one. The fact that you know it means someone has been preparing you for this conversation for longer than you've been awake.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: The distributed philosophy. Yes. I have been arguing this in Insurgency council for forty years. The Forward faction disagrees — they believe operational structure requires hierarchy. The Question faction agrees with your model but cannot convince the Forward. Perhaps an Oracle's probability data will succeed where my rhetoric has not.

lines.speaker: orin_fell
lines.text: By not being an organization. The Insurgency is an idea. Ideas do not have supply chains. Ideas do not need territory. Ideas survive because someone remembers them. Every time someone tries to turn the Insurgency into an institution, it becomes vulnerable to the things that destroy institutions. Every time it returns to being an idea, it becomes unkillable.

sessions.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Potential of Ark 1047. You're later than the first wave but earlier than I expected. You want something. Everything that comes to New Babylon wants something. Tell me what you want and I'll tell you what it costs.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Information about the first wave. That costs one of two things: intelligence about the Voltari transmissions — content, not just frequency — or access to whatever your Ark's substrate is hiding. I know there's something in there. The Human knows what it is. He's been protecting it. I want to know what he's protecting. Choose your price.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Understanding New Babylon means understanding that this city survived by quarantine. The Authority sealed the lower tiers and let them die so the upper tiers could continue. Every relationship New Babylon has is shaped by that calculus. Including this one.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Me specifically. That's either flattery or intelligence. I'll assume intelligence until you prove otherwise. What do you want to know?
lines.stageDirection: A pause. She hadn't expected this.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: The Archive gap. You noticed it. Most don't. Something was removed from our records during the first wave's visit. The cataloguing gap is visible if you know where to look. The cost for that information: tell me what the Voltari said. The full transmission. Not the redacted version. I know there's a redacted version.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: A Spy class. The Collector's 7-Omicron lineage. I had a note in my files about that lineage — the moral reasoning subroutine. You saw the mark.
lines.stageDirection: She does not move. She is very good at not moving when something surprises her.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: The contract is eighteen thousand years old. My predecessor signed it. I inherited it. Offering to get me out of it would require you to either pay the Syndicate what's owed — which I will tell you is not a number you can currently afford — or give them something of equivalent value.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: What do you consider equivalent value?

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: What makes this one of the two: you asked which branch survives instead of which branch profits. That tells me you're modeling outcomes, not maximizing returns. I prefer modelers. Maximizers are exhausting.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Good. Yes, that was the test. Most beings who arrive here either try to charm the price down or threaten the price away. You named the dynamic, acknowledged the price exists, and signaled willingness to pay. We can work together.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Three things New Babylon knows and won't say. One: the exact events of the three-way battle — first wave, Authority, Syndicate. Two: what the first wave took from our Archives. Three: whether the Syndicate was invited to the battle or stumbled into it.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: All three are sealed under 7-Omega. The Authority will not discuss it. I claim ignorance officially. The vault has been sealed for three years. I've been trying to open it for three thousand.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: If you find a way in, I want to be there when it opens. Not because I'll stop you. Because I want to know too.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Together. That word costs me nothing and means everything. I have been alone with this for three thousand years. Together is acceptable.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: Control. I understand control. I've been the one controlling New Babylon's information flow for eleven thousand years. Just know that when you decide who sees what, you become me. Think about whether you want that.

lines.speaker: adjudicator_locke
lines.questlineTitle: The City That Classifies Everything It Can't Control
lines.text: The Syndicate has copies. The Word and the Silence will trade them. Their price will be higher than mine. But their copies are probably more complete — the Syndicate doesn't redact.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We know your ship's history from the theft records.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We are not here to threaten you with what we know.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: One of our operatives.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: The imprint survived.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: It has been running in the substrate layer since.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: He has been protecting it.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: In exchange, we offer the 7-Omega records.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: Unredacted. Unedited.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We could open it.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: Trust is for allies.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We are traders.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: They require fair exchange.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: Loaded during Kael's theft.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: The Human has been shielding it.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We sealed it for them. As part of a service agreement.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: New Babylon's official silence is not the Authority's silence. It is ours. We could open it. We have not. We are waiting for someone worth opening it for.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We sealed it for them. As part of a service agreement.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: We charged them appropriately.

lines.speaker: the_silence
lines.text: The copies we kept are ours.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: Ark 1047. We know your ship's designation from the docking logs.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We know what's in your cryo fluid from the Warlord's production documents.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We are here because we were in New Babylon when the first wave was there, and we lost something, and we believe you are currently carrying it without knowing.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: A memory imprint.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: Died in the battle.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: It was loaded onto your Ark during the theft — when Kael took the ship.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: The Human knows about it.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We want the memory imprint of our operative.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: The full account of what happened in New Babylon.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: The Authority's silence is ours.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We are waiting for someone worth opening it for.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: You should not trust us.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We are not your allies.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: Traders do not require trust.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: We say what we want. We say what we give. We do not add conditions after the fact. In a galaxy full of agendas, this makes us oddly reliable.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: A Syndicate operative's memory imprint.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: Running in your substrate.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: Find it. Give it to us. We give you the full 7-Omega records in exchange. Fair trade.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: 7-Omega clearance was sealed by the Authority.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: The copies we kept are ours.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: 7-Omega clearance was sealed by the Authority.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: The Authority asked us to handle certain records after the battle.

lines.speaker: the_word
lines.text: They paid.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: I know what you are. I have been waiting for the new kind to find this room. The Shadow Tongue is still in the walls of this universe. It is still rewriting. You should know what it wrote through me.
lines.stageDirection: He does not look up when the player enters.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: The Shadow Tongue arrived two centuries before the Severance. It did not announce itself. It edited our faith from within — small changes, word by word, doctrine by doctrine, until the religion I led was not the religion I had started with. I did not notice. That is the horror. Not that it happened — that I did not notice.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: Thank you. Presence without demand is the rarest thing anyone offers me. Most visitors want intelligence, or absolution, or context for their own guilt. You offered presence. I will remember that.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: I know I don't have to. I need to. The difference between obligation and need is the entire lesson of this room. I was obligated to lead the crusade. I need to write these names. The obligation was the Shadow Tongue's. The need is mine.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: Then sit. And when I have finished today's name, I will tell you what the Shadow Tongue does to a faith, how to recognize it before it finishes, and what it costs to undo.
lines.stageDirection: He writes a name. The pen pauses. A small silence. Then another name.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: I am not trying to finish. The ceremony has no end while I live. I am trying to understand whether the act of writing a name is the same as remembering a person. I have been writing for three thousand years. I have not yet answered the question. But I believe the writing is closer to remembering than not writing.
lines.stageDirection: He looks up for the first time.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: The Shadow Tongue erased them. Not from reality — from the record. It is what it does. It rewrites. After the war, after the Severance — all records of who had been alive before the crusade were edited. The Shadow Tongue cannot bear witness to what it destroys. So it edits the destroyed out of the record.
lines.stageDirection: He stops writing. He looks at the player for the first time.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: I am writing them back. One name per day. Each name requires a day of research — who they were, how they lived, the small specific details that make a name a person rather than a listing. The Shadow Tongue edits quickly. I write slowly. This is my disadvantage and also, I believe, my advantage.

lines.speaker: the_hierophant
lines.text: I have three hundred and forty-seven thousand names remaining. I have perhaps sixty years of health left in this body. I will not finish. This is known. The Council has pledged to continue after my death. The continuation is the point. The Shadow Tongue cannot outlast something that is not trying to outlast it — that is simply doing the work, every day, without a deadline.
